metadata.title: Understanding teacher ICT usage: Insights from ICILS 2018 Korea data

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses ICILS 2018 teacher questionnaire data collected via an online 30-minute teacher survey, following IEA sampling, data collection, and coding procedures. The manuscript does not report whether complex survey sampling weights or replicate weights were applied in the analysis. Because the analysis is conducted using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS4 (rather than PV-based achievement modeling), the paper does not specify any weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight scheme. Analysts using the ICILS microdata should consult the ICILS user guide for the appropriate teacher weight and replicate weights (if provided) and apply them when estimating uncertainty; however, this paper’s weighting strategy is not documented.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the dependent variables are teachers’ ICT usage constructs (e.g., ICTPRAC, USETOOL, USEUTIL) derived from questionnaire items and modeled via PLS-SEM, not cognitive achievement scores that are typically PV-based in ILSA student assessments. Missing data handling is reported: the authors state that missingness is small (maximum 3.6%) and that mean imputation was used to replace missing values.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analysis is restricted to Korea as a case study using ICILS 2018 teacher questionnaire data. The authors exclude specific questionnaire items: Q4 (teaching at multiple schools), Q8 (subject for reference class), Q10 (students’ ICT use frequency), and Q16 (initial teacher education duration elements). They also combine items from Q6 with Q5 to form EXP and combine T_PROFSTR and T_PROFREC into PD. For the analytic dataset, mean imputation is applied to missing values (maximum 3.6% per variable), and the remaining constructs are built from the ICILS item sets after removing the specified items and additional items removed to satisfy the measurement model (7A, 7B, 7D from ICTEFF; 12I from USETOOL; 18D from VWNEG).

main_findings.dataset_used: ICILS 2018 Teacher questionnaire (Korea) — teacher ICT usage constructs
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM path coefficients (direct effects): COLICT→ICTPRAC β=0.082, t=3.197, p=0.001; PD→ICTPRAC β=0.129, t=5.083, p<0.001; ICTEMP→ICTPRAC β=0.206, t=8.42, p<0.001; CODEMP→ICTPRAC β=0.233, t=9.535, p<0.001; ICTEFF→ICTPRAC β=0.067, t=3.21, p=0.001; EXP→ICTPRAC β=0.177, t=9.304, p<0.001; VWNEG→ICTPRAC β=-0.005, t=0.199, p=0.842. Total effects: COLICT→ICTPRAC β=0.261, t=9.732, p<0.001; PD→ICTPRAC β=0.278, t=12.313, p<0.001; ICTEFF→ICTPRAC β=0.067, t=3.21, p=0.001; VWNEG→ICTPRAC β=-0.005, t=0.199, p=0.842.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICILS 2018 teacher questionnaire data from Korea, the study leveraged Professional development (PD), Teacher ICT collaboration (COLICT), Emphasis on ICT capabilities (ICTEMP), Emphasis on coding tasks (CODEMP), and Prior ICT experience (EXP) to model ICTPRAC (ICT use for assessment practices) in a three-layer PLS-SEM structure, finding that most external and internal constructs significantly predict ICTPRAC while school ICT resources (RESRC) show no direct effect. This indicates that strengthening teacher collaboration and professional development may be more effective than relying on school-level ICT resources alone for increasing teachers’ ICT use in assessment-related practices, though the study is correlational and does not establish causal effects.

main_findings.dataset_used: ICILS 2018 Teacher questionnaire (Korea) — teacher ICT usage constructs
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM direct effects: COLICT→USETOOL β=0.095, t=3.952, p<0.001; PD→USETOOL β=0.305, t=9.877, p<0.001; RESRC→USETOOL β=0.019, t=0.813, p=0.417 (ns); ICTEMP→USETOOL β=0.156, t=7.191, p<0.001; CODEMP→USETOOL β=0.179, t=7.361, p<0.001; ICTEFF→USETOOL β=0.012, t=0.586, p=0.558 (ns); EXP→USETOOL β=-0.011, t=0.574, p=0.566 (ns); VWNEG→USETOOL β=0.086, t=2.872, p=0.004. Total effects: COLICT→USETOOL β=0.210, t=8.422, p<0.001; PD→USETOOL β=0.386, t=14.397, p<0.001; ICTEMP→USETOOL β=0.156, t=7.191, p<0.001; CODEMP→USETOOL β=0.179, t=7.361, p<0.001; VWNEG→USETOOL β=0.086, t=2.872, p=0.004; ICTEFF→USETOOL β=0.012, t=0.586, p=0.558 (ns); EXP→USETOOL β=-0.011, t=0.574, p=0.566 (ns).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICILS 2018 teacher questionnaire data from Korea, the study leveraged Professional development (PD), Teacher ICT collaboration (COLICT), Emphasis on ICT capabilities (ICTEMP), Emphasis on coding tasks (CODEMP), and Negative views on ICT (VWNEG) to model USETOOL (use of digital learning tools) in a three-layer PLS-SEM structure, finding that PD and COLICT have strong positive direct and total effects while school ICT resources (RESRC) and general ICT self-efficacy (ICTEFF) do not directly predict USETOOL. This indicates that targeted professional learning and peer collaboration may be key levers for translating teachers’ ICT attitudes and capabilities into actual use of specific digital learning tools, though the model does not provide causal identification.

main_findings.dataset_used: ICILS 2018 Teacher questionnaire (Korea) — teacher ICT usage constructs
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM direct effects: COLICT→USEUTIL β=0.063, t=2.552, p=0.011; PD→USEUTIL β=0.089, t=3.692, p<0.001; RESRC→USEUTIL β=-0.026, t=1.232, p=0.218 (ns); ICTEMP→USEUTIL β=0.123, t=5.148, p<0.001; CODEMP→USEUTIL β=0.126, t=5.559, p<0.001; ICTEFF→USEUTIL β=0.097, t=4.9, p<0.001; EXP→USEUTIL β=0.322, t=18.428, p<0.001; VWNEG→USEUTIL β=-0.051, t=2.532, p=0.011. Total effects: COLICT→USEUTIL β=0.204, t=7.565, p<0.001; PD→USEUTIL β=0.220, t=9.349, p<0.001; ICTEFF→USEUTIL β=0.097, t=4.9, p<0.001; EXP→USEUTIL β=0.322, t=18.428, p<0.001; VWNEG→USEUTIL β=-0.051, t=2.532, p=0.011; RESRC→USEUTIL β=-0.002, t=0.087, p=0.931 (ns).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICILS 2018 teacher questionnaire data from Korea, the study leveraged Professional development (PD), Teacher ICT collaboration (COLICT), Emphasis on ICT capabilities (ICTEMP), Prior ICT experience (EXP), and Negative views on ICT (VWNEG) to model USEUTIL (use of general utility software) in a three-layer PLS-SEM structure, finding that experience and ICT-related attitudes (including negative views) significantly relate to utility-software use while school ICT resources (RESRC) do not. This indicates that professional learning and collaboration should be complemented with experience-building opportunities and attention to teachers’ negative perceptions to increase routine use of general ICT tools, while recognizing that the study’s design is correlational rather than causal.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes ICILS 2018 teacher questionnaire data and uses Korea as a case study (N=2127 teachers) to test a three-layer model (external factors, internal factors, and an action layer) using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS4 with 10,000 bootstraps. The dependent constructs are teachers’ ICT usage: ICTPRAC (assessment-related ICT use), USETOOL (digital learning tools), and USEUTIL (general utility software). Across the action layer, most external and internal constructs show significant direct and total effects, with PD and COLICT consistently predicting all three usage outcomes; RESRC (school ICT resources) shows no direct effects on any action-layer construct. Key path coefficients include PD→USETOOL β=0.305 (t=9.877, p<0.001) and EXP→USEUTIL β=0.322 (t=18.428, p<0.001). Missing data were handled via mean imputation (max 3.6% per variable), and the authors note that causal relationships are not thoroughly considered.
